skill.name: prd
skill.description: Generate structured Product Requirements Documents for software systems and AI-powered features, including discovery questions, user stories, technical specifications, risks, and measurable success criteria.
skill.summary: Create structured PRDs for software systems, AI features, user stories, technical specs, risks, and success criteria.
skill.author: github

security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged Markdown backticks and a quality-guidance sentence, but the reviewed context shows PRD documentation examples rather than executable commands or reconnaissance. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or hidden malicious behavior was found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - **User Stories**: `As a [user], I want to [action] so that [benefit].`
- **Hallucinate Constraints**: If the user didn't specify a tech stack, ask or label it as `TBD`.
Use concrete, measurable criteria. Avoid "fast", "easy", or "intuitive".

finding_verdicts.reason: The finding points to a Markdown diff code fence used to show vague versus concrete requirements examples. It does not execute Ruby, shell, or any command.
The line closes the Markdown code fence opened for a requirements-quality example. There is no executable command invocation or user-controlled shell input.
The backticks wrap a user-story template as inline Markdown text. This is documentation formatting and not command execution.
The backticks wrap the placeholder text TBD in a writing guideline. It is not shell syntax and does not instruct the agent to run a command.
The line lists example tool names inside inline Markdown for a sample PRD architecture section. It describes possible requirements content and does not direct the agent to invoke external commands.
The line is a writing-quality instruction to use measurable criteria. It contains no reconnaissance behavior, system probing, or request for host information.

content.value_statement: Teams often lose time turning product ideas into clear engineering requirements. This skill guides discovery and produces structured PRDs with measurable scope, risks, and acceptance criteria.
actual_capabilities: Asks discovery questions before drafting a PRD.
Structures PRDs with executive summary, user experience, technical specifications, risks, and roadmap sections.
Defines measurable success criteria and acceptance criteria.
Includes AI system requirements when the product includes AI features.
Separates goals, non-goals, dependencies, and risks for clearer scope.
limitations: Requires user-provided product context before it can produce a useful PRD.
Does not validate market demand or business priority independently.
Does not replace legal, security, or compliance review for regulated products.
May leave unknown technical details as TBD when the user has not supplied them.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Feature
use_cases.description: Turn a product idea into a structured PRD with user stories, acceptance criteria, and launch scope.

use_cases.title: Align Engineering Scope
use_cases.description: Create technical specifications, dependencies, non-goals, and risks before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Define AI Product Requirements
use_cases.description: Document model behavior, evaluation strategy, tool requirements, privacy concerns, and quality targets for AI features.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic PRD
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a clear first draft.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PRD for this feature: [feature idea]. Ask me at least two clarifying questions before drafting.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Existing Requirements
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve rough notes into a more complete document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these notes into a PRD with user stories, acceptance criteria, non-goals, and success metrics: [notes].

prompt_templates.title: Plan an AI Feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Document requirements for a product that uses AI.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a PRD for an AI-powered feature. Include evaluation strategy, data handling, quality risks, and measurable KPIs.

prompt_templates.title: Review PRD Completeness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this PRD for missing scope, weak acceptance criteria, unclear risks, and unmeasurable success metrics: [PRD text].

output_examples.input: Create a PRD for intelligent documentation search.
output_examples.output: A PRD with a problem statement, proposed solution, success metrics, user stories, acceptance criteria, technical architecture, risks, and rollout phases.

output_examples.input: Turn these rough checkout notes into product requirements.
output: Clarifying questions about users, payment constraints, and success metrics.
A structured requirements document with non-goals and measurable acceptance criteria.

output_examples.input: Review this AI feature PRD before engineering planning.
output_examples.output: A gap analysis covering missing evaluation criteria, privacy concerns, unclear dependencies, and suggested revisions.

best_practices: Provide product goals, target users, constraints, and known dependencies before asking for the final PRD.
Ask for measurable acceptance criteria and success metrics for each major requirement.
Review the draft with product, engineering, design, security, and data stakeholders.
anti_patterns: Do not request a final PRD from a vague idea without answering discovery questions.
Do not treat generated technical assumptions as approved architecture decisions.
Do not skip non-goals, risks, or evaluation criteria for complex features.

faq.question: What kind of PRD does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates structured PRDs for software systems and AI-powered features, including scope, user stories, technical details, risks, and metrics.

faq.question: Does it ask questions before drafting?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill instructs the assistant to ask clarifying questions before producing a complete PRD.

faq.question: Can it handle AI product requirements?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes sections for AI tool requirements, evaluation strategy, data handling, and output quality.

faq.question: Can it make engineering decisions for my team?
faq.answer: No. It can document options and assumptions, but your team should confirm architecture, constraints, and implementation choices.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the core problem, target users, desired outcomes, constraints, dependencies, timeline, and any known technical requirements.

faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
